newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shippers seek govt enquiry on fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shippers seek govt enquiry on fuel surcharge.

text.p: EVO, the Dutch shippers association, is writing to the Dutch government Monday calling for an investigation into alleged "coordinated carrier action" regarding the imposition of fuel surcharges.
Hans Leijgraaff, EVO secretary, said the association is writing to the Competition Department of the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
"Fuel surcharges seem to have been imposed between November 1-6 or on November 15, at levels of 10 U.S. cents per kilo by nearly all of the carriers," suggesting a coordinated action said Leijgraaff.
"We will urge the Competition authority to investigate the issue as soon as possible. There has been a snowball effect as more carriers introduce surcharges."
Since November 1, when KLM Cargo, the Dutch national carrier, introduced a 20 guilder cents per kilo surcharge,many carriers have followed suit.
EVO has received 15 official notices of fuel surcharges and is aware of another 5 carriers introducing them, covering all the major market sectors.

"An investigation is obviously going to be time consuming but EVO remains optimistic," Leijgraaff said, adding that two years ago a similar action by the carriers was stopped. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
